evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Token F1 and BLEU-1 are external lexical-overlap metrics that corroborate the LLM-Judge quality gains across both backbones.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LoCoMo answer quality scores are measured with an LLM Judge, token F1, and BLEU-1 against dialogue-derived reference answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: RIME is an untrained architectural memory pipeline that uses fixed generic formation questions, frozen text embeddings, and TF-IDF retrieval without task-specific parameter optimization.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior memory quality, reduced query-time token costs compared to deliberative baselines, and the modular importance of write-time retrieval and read-time fallback are well supported by experimental tables.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated on the standard LoCoMo benchmark (1,540 non-adversarial questions) across two LLM backbones against relevant baselines (RAG, Mem0, A-MEM, Nemori, D-Mem), measuring LLM-Judge, F1, BLEU-1, and inference tokens alongside comprehensive ablations.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard n-gram lexical overlap metrics (token F1 and BLEU-1) objectively corroborate the LLM-Judge quality improvements across both backbones.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LoCoMo evaluation scores measuring answer accuracy using an LLM Judge, F1 score, and BLEU-1 against reference dialogue answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The memory system is an untuned architectural pipeline using fixed generic prompt queries, frozen text embeddings, and TF-IDF without learned task-specific parameter optimization.

primary.limitations: The evaluation excludes the adversarial split of LoCoMo and relies on a fixed set of six generic formation queries, while write-time token overhead during memory construction is not explicitly quantified alongside query tokens.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly specified with explicit mathematical formulations for question-guided retrieval, context expansion, memory bank operations (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP), and fallback source dialogue retrieval via TF-IDF.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped architectural contribution to LLM agent memory systems with sound technical details and rigorous comparative benchmarking against standard baselines.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RIME, a long-term dialogue memory framework for LLM agents that uses generic question-guided evidence retrieval prior to memory consolidation and selective source-dialogue fallback at query time.
